title: Add traceable supplier-payment allocations to Purchase Orders
description: Add an explicit allocation register between existing supplier-payment evidence and Purchase Orders so users can record which orders a payment document refers to without creating or executing a payment. Reuse the repository's existing supplier-payment document and Purchase Order records; do not create a second payment master, infer allocations, mark invoices or orders as settled, move funds, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Users can maintain bounded allocation rows for an existing non-deleted supplier-payment document, each referencing one existing non-cancelled Purchase Order and recording an allocation amount plus bounded notes.

The server validates authoritative Supplier and currency compatibility between the payment evidence and every Purchase Order; mismatches are rejected and are never converted, reassigned or matched by number, text, date or amount similarity.

The sum of active allocation rows cannot exceed the authoritative payment-evidence amount, currency precision is enforced server-side, and duplicate active links to the same Purchase Order within one payment document are rejected.
Allocation rows preserve bounded payment, Supplier, Purchase Order and currency snapshots so historical evidence remains identifiable when a referenced master record later becomes unavailable.
Users can void an incorrect allocation with a reason while preserving its original values and history; hard deletion, silent replacement and rewriting of previously voided evidence are not provided.
The workflow clearly labels allocations as payment-reference evidence rather than proof of bank transfer, accounts-payable settlement, invoice discharge, tax eligibility or Supplier balance.

Creating or voiding an allocation does not change the payment document's approval or execution status, Purchase Order status, receipt progress, invoice records, inventory cost, Supplier balance, expenses or tax records.
Existing payment documents and Purchase Orders remain readable without allocation rows, and no request-time or production backfill is performed.
List and detail queries are bounded or paged and avoid per-row database queries; repository schema changes are idempotent and validated only through permitted local or test-database paths.

Unit/integration tests cover full and partial allocation, multiple orders, Supplier and currency mismatch, over-allocation, duplicate links, void history, legacy records, bounded queries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Open an existing supplier-payment document, allocate part of its amount to two compatible Purchase Orders, and verify the traceable rows and remaining unallocated evidence without changing either order.

Attempt a Supplier or currency mismatch and an over-allocation, verify they are rejected, then void a valid allocation and verify its history remains visible without presenting the payment as settled.

human_gate.reason: Repository allocation evidence and non-production test schema only. Real payment execution, production database changes, irreversible finance operations, deployment and release remain behind mandatory human gates.
